title: Privileged Identity & Keying PRD: scoped sign-off and acceptance checklist
creator: Marina Kline
description: This PRD defines the minimal and recommended security requirements for Private and Dedicated customers focused on identity, role management, audit trail completeness, and key lifecycle controls. The goal is a clear, testable acceptance checklist that maps to engineering deliverables and compliance checkbox items for SOC2/ISO considerations. It targets SSO/SAML integration patterns, fine-grained RBAC for control plane and data plane actions, immutable audit logging schema, and KMS/HSM usage patterns for secret and model key material. Deliverables include API contracts, console UX copy for admin flows, telemetry events for audits, and operator runbooks for key rotation and incident handling.
scope: In-scope: SSO via SAML/OIDC with IdP metadata import and SCIM provisioning; RBAC roles and permission matrix for console and API; audit log schema (immutable, signed, exportable); KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM via PKCS#11); key rotation and envelope encryption for model artifacts. Out-of-scope: full IAM federation with cloud providers (deferred to future work), per-token hardware attestation, and custom proprietary HSM appliances requiring on-prem driver development.
non_goals: Do not assume a single universal RBAC model for every enterprise—provide a mapping guide and extensibility hooks. Do not design a new KMS service—integrations only. Do not ship cryptographic primitives; use vetted libraries and platform KMS/HSM.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Tenant admin can upload SAML metadata and validate single-sign-on end-to-end using a test IdP within the console; automated smoke test demonstrates assertion exchange and session creation.
SCIM: Provisioning events (create/update/deactivate) from IdP are processed and surfaced in user listings within 60s; SCIM errors are tracked in Retry queue with operator alerting.
RBAC: Pre-defined roles (owner, admin, observer, operator, app-service) exist and can be assigned via console and API; API access tokens honor role permissions and return 403 on forbidden actions.

Audit logs: All admin-sensitive operations (auth config changes, RBAC grants, KMS binding changes, key rotations, private deployment upgrades) produce structured events with immutable IDs, timestamps in ISO8601, and actor metadata; logs are tamper-evident (append-only storage + HMAC signing) and exportable in JSONL.

KMS: Customers can register an external KMS resource by providing connection metadata; Redwood can encrypt model artifacts using envelope encryption and rotate data keys without downtime; integration tests against AWS KMS and a PKCS#11 emulator pass.
Key rotation and incident playbook: There is an operator runbook that documents rotating data-encryption keys, revoking access grants, and verifying integrity of encrypted artifacts with a checklist.

Telemetry: Events for SSO configuration, failed/locked sign-ins, RBAC changes, KMS errors, and key rotations are visible in Console security dashboard and exported to customer SIEM via webhook/CloudWatch/Stackdriver endpoints.
Documentation: Admin guide, API reference, and runbooks published with example cURL/SDK flows and least-privilege recommendations.
Security review: Completed by Security team and findings closed or deferred with compensating controls documented.

rollout_plan: Staged rollout: 1) Internal dogfooding on staging with Redwood SSO tenant and mocked KMS 2) Invite-only beta with three enterprise customers (security NDAs completed) 3) GA on private and dedicated deployments with opt-in toggle for existing customers. Rollout includes feature flags for KMS integration and audit signing; GA gated on 3rd-party KMS test coverage and runbook signoff.
test_plan: Unit tests for RBAC enforcement across read/write admin APIs
Integration smoke test: upload SAML metadata -> initiate SSO -> create session
End-to-end KMS integration test using AWS KMS test keys and PKCS#11 emulator
Audit log integrity test: append events -> validate HMAC chain and export
Chaos test: simulate KMS unavailability and verify graceful fallback and customer-visible error
Performance test: ensure audit logging path does not add >5ms p95 to admin API calls
decisions: 2025-02-20: Use envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS keys by default for private deployments (decided after threat modeling).
2025-02-25: Adopt SCIM v2 for provisioning; remove proprietary sync agent from initial scope to reduce surface area.
2025-03-01: Audit log storage will be append-only in S3 with HMAC signing by a cluster key rotated quarterly; HSM-backed signing deferred to H2 roadmap.
2025-03-04: RBAC will ship with a fixed set of curated roles and an extensible custom-role API; custom role UI deferred to GA+1.
